findings.title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` overload
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Existing callers that pass `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` will now bind `max_width` to `dimensions` and `max_height` (an integer) to `opts`, causing `opts[:allow_animation]` in `self.optimize` to raise `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`, while callers passing 5 arguments `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` will raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

findings.title: `tempfile.size` and `tempfile` become stale after `ImageOptim` replaces `tempfile.path`
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` calls `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)`, which writes optimized output to a temporary file and atomically renames it over `tempfile.path`. However, `tempfile` is an open `Tempfile` object whose underlying file descriptor still points to the original (now unlinked) inode, and `tempfile.size` calls `fstat` on that open descriptor rather than checking `File.size(tempfile.path)`. Once `ImageOptim` replaces the file on the first iteration, subsequent iterations modify the new inode at `tempfile.path` while `tempfile.size` never changes, causing the loop to run all 5 attempts unnecessarily and pass the stale `tempfile` descriptor and old `tempfile.size` to `Upload.create_for` (which can still fail the size check or record the wrong file size).

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing fails when given a percentage dimension like `"80%"`
findings.body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. For a `.gif` file with `allow_animation` enabled, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` flag only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (percentage scaling in `gifsicle` requires `--scale`), so `gifsicle` exits with an error on all 5 attempts and animated GIFs are never downsized.

findings.title: Hardcoding `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` breaks attachment size validation and ignores site settings above 10MB
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` validates both `'image'` and `'attachment'` uploads, previously checking `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Hardcoding `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` stops checking `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image attachments—which are not downsized by the server and will be rejected only after the upload finishes—and also blocks uploads larger than 10MB when an administrator has configured `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB.
